# A streamed markdown document can end unlike its one-shot parse

Sub of #21367: an engine defect before More components' markdown card (#21474).

## Context

On `dev` 32d592f333, the stream demo of `examples/component/markdown` (24-character chunks of its source) ends in another document than "Render instantly" from a cleared state:

- `## Why transcripts need this` renders as a heading "Why tran" and a paragraph "scripts need this".
- The table has no head: its `<table>` holds the old paragraph's text node `| Surface | Layer | |---|` beside the body rows (DOM read in the browser, 19 Nov: children of `TABLE#…__md-7` are the comment `…__md-7-c0`, `TBODY#…__md-7-c6` and that text).

Streaming LLM transcripts is what the component is for, so the example's demo shows the defect to everyone who presses its first button.

## The Problem

Three faults in `src/component/markdown/Parser.mjs`, each reproduced in a unit spec:

1. `#segment` gives headings and breaks `open: false` even when their line is the unfinished last line, so a chunk boundary inside a heading settles it.
2. The empty string after a final `\n` counts as a blank line, so a paragraph, list, quote or table that ends in a newline settles before its next line arrives. A table header row then never meets its delimiter row.
3. `#appendParse` reuses the tail's id when the tail changes block type (paragraph → table), and child ids are numbered in creation order (`-c0`, `-c1`), so a re-parse hands one node's id to a node of another kind. The differ matches by id and keeps the old text node where the `thead` belongs. The same shift happens inside one growing block when an unclosed `**` turns into `strong` or a padded table cell fills.

## The Architectural Reality

Design authority: the parser's header, "Block sequence numbers never recycle — not within a value lifetime and not across resets — so a reset cannot birth two-nodes-one-id across batches", and its streaming model, in which only the open tail block re-parses.

- `Parser.mjs`: `#segment`, `#appendParse`, `#createBlock` (the child id dispenser), `#parseInline`.
- `blockMeta.open` feeds the component's virtualization: an open block's `units` can still change.
- `test/playwright/unit/component/markdown/Parser.spec.mjs` pins "a streamed table promotes from the open tail paragraph when its delimiter arrives" with the paragraph's id on the table.

## The Fix

- A heading or break stays open while its line is unfinished. A block that reaches the empty string after a final newline stays open, and its source keeps that newline, so the next append continues the exact suffix.
- A tail that turns into another block type becomes a new block under a fresh id.
- A child id carries its node's kind (`-t3`, `-li0`, `-strong2`), so no id can name two kinds of node.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: For chunk sizes 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 11 and 24, streaming a document with every block type ends in the same blocks as its one-shot parse.
- [ ] AC-2: Across a stream, no id names two kinds of node.
- [ ] AC-3: The markdown example's stream demo renders "Why transcripts need this" as one heading and its table with a head.
- [ ] AC-4: The markdown unit specs and `MarkdownStreamingCoherenceNL.spec.mjs` pass.

## Out of Scope

- The markdown card in More components (#21474).
- The VDOM differ.

## Avoided Traps

- Teaching the differ to replace a node whose id changes kind: the producer that gives one id to two kinds is at fault, and a differ that matches by id is right to trust ids.
